title: AI Solutions Program Manager, Finance
description:
Who we are  

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

You'll be joining the Finance Operational Excellence team, reporting to the Head of Finance Operational Excellence. We are finance transformation and AI experts working side-by-side with Finance, Product, and Engineering teams to redefine processes and build the finance organization of the future. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys working across disciplines: part solution developer, part data architect, part workflow designer, and part coach. You’ll have room to shape how applied AI is built and scaled both from a technical and end-user perspective.

What you’ll do

You'll work side-by-side with Finance subject matter experts to understand how work gets done, identify the highest impact opportunities, and partner with domain teams to chart a transformation plan which balances future ambitions with rapid impact.  You'll work independently to automate manual processes, design and build agents and required data solutions using internal platforms, and enable Finance teams to maintain these solutions long-term. 

You’ll build with your partner teams, not simply deliver solutions to them. You’ll help colleagues move from a manual workflow, to a first AI-enabled win, to a reliable solution they can confidently operate and improve themselves. Success means the workflow stays transformed after the initial build, the team trusts the output, and the people closest to the process can own what comes next. 

You’ll favor learning through building. When possible, you’ll put a useful prototype in front of a Finance user, test it against a real deliverable, and improve it quickly rather than spend weeks describing a theoretical future state. When you encounter platform limitations—which you will—you’ll find creative, supportable approaches, collaborate with Engineering to scope and test custom tools, and escalate strategically when needed.

This role requires a blend of process automation, data operations, technical problem-solving, and stakeholder enablement. You'll spend your time building agents, optimizing data pipelines that feed them, creating knowledge layers that make them more accurate, and training Finance teams to use and maintain them. Success means Finance teams can independently run agents you've built while you provide light support and focus on the next automation opportunity.

Responsibilities

  • Embed with Finance teams to diagnose workflows, identify high-leverage opportunities, and translate business, data, and control requirements into practical AI and automation solutions.
  • Build and operationalize AI agents for Finance use cases, delivering end-to-end solutions from prototype through validation, monitoring, documentation, and handoff.
  • Write and optimize SQL for data extraction, transformation, calculation, and validation, ensuring Finance-facing outputs are accurate, explainable, and reliable.
  • Design reusable knowledge layers, evaluation methods, validation patterns, data-quality frameworks, and components that improve agent accuracy and accelerate future use cases.
  • Identify agentic limitations and new possibilities; determine when to use existing capabilities, develop an alternative approach, or partner with Engineering to scope and test custom tools and integrations, including tools using Model Context Protocol where appropriate.
  • Build alongside users, gather feedback through real deliverables, and iterate until the solution fits the workflow and earns user trust.
  • Enable long-term ownership through clear SOPs, runbooks, training, and self-service tooling; coach Finance teams to operate, maintain, and evolve what has been built.
  • Establish monitoring and observability for deployed agents, including metrics, alerting, and incident-response processes that support reliable operation.
  • Diagnose technical and data issues, resolve problems independently where possible, and collaborate with Engineering when solutions require deeper platform changes.
  • Measure adoption and impact, share lessons and wins, and turn successful implementations into standards, components, and playbooks for the broader Finance AI portfolio.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in data analytics, technical operations, business intelligence, automation, solutions delivery, or a related field.
  • Of which, 2+ years of experience in program management, working directly alongside business leaders to develop and execute process transformation programs
  • Hands-on experience building AI-enabled tools, agents, automations, or workflows that changed a real business process—not solely using AI as a conversational tool, 
  • Strong SQL proficiency, including experience writing complex queries using CTEs, window functions, and joins for data analysis, transformation, or pipeline logic.
  • A track record of independently scoping and delivering technical solutions for process improvement, demonstrating ownership from problem definition through adoption.
  • Strong analytical and investigative skills, including the ability to identify root causes, debug complex data problems, and resolve inconsistencies.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and work effectively with domain experts and Engineering partners.
  • Experience teaching, coaching, enabling users, or transferring ownership of a solution through documentation, training, or self-service tools.
  • Working knowledge of development practices such as version control, testing, code review, and iterative delivery.
  • Experience using low-code tools, scripting, workflow automation, AI-assisted development, or custom integrations, paired with curiosity and the ability to learn evolving technologies.

You will also likely have (not required):

  • Domain experience in Finance Operations, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Payments, or other areas.
  • Familiarity with modern data tools and practices, such as Python, Databricks, ETL/ELT processes, data pipelines, and data-quality controls.
  • Experience with Model Context Protocol or another extensibility or integration framework.
  • Experience navigating financial systems and understanding how data flows through accounting, reporting, reconciliation, forecasting, or payments processes.
  • Experience with change management, organizational transformation, or large-scale enablement programs.
  • Experience building internal tools, templates, components, or playbooks that were adopted beyond the original team or use case.
  • Experience working in a high-growth technology company with rapidly evolving processes and tools.

Note on technical depth: This role involves working at the intersection of no-code AI tools and custom development. While software engineering expertise is not required, you should be comfortable applying technical concepts, collaborating closely with Engineering teams, and using AI-assisted development tools to extend platform capabilities when needed.

We train frontier models that learn the underlying foundations of biochemical structure and interaction, so scientists can move faster and pursue targets that other methods cannot reach. AI is reinventing life sciences the same way it reinvented software engineering, and Chai is at the forefront of this shift. Leading pharmaceutical companies like Eli Lilly , Pfizer , and Novartis are adopting our platform to power their drug discovery programs. We value diverse perspectives and are ready to find greatness in unexpected places. About the role We are making our first finance hire. Someone we can trust to own Chai's financial operating system end to end. Chai is a small, fast-growing company with complex financial operations; heavy spend on compute and data acquisition; and pharmaceutical partnerships with complex revenue recognition and compliance requirements. We need someone who can make sure the machinery underneath the business is exceptionally well run, and give us the visibility to make good decisions as we scale. You will own the quality of our books and close process, build a trusted view of where our money is going, and take over the financial model and cash forecast. You'll manage accounting and finance vendors, improve all systems and controls, and lead our audit readiness. Once the foundations are in place, we expect your attention will turn towards strategic questions: allocating capital, modeling major investments, negotiating important relationships, and generally supporting key decisions as we grow. About you You are a financial generalist who combines operational rigor with strong financial judgment. You are sophisticated enough to understand the entire financial picture of the company, but hands-on enough to personally chase down a strange invoice, manage an accounting firm, negotiate a vendor renewal, or rebuild a cash forecast. Nothing is beneath you if it matters to the business. You likely have meaningful experience inside a startup. You may have been an early finance hire or second-in-command at a high-growth technology company, come from strategic finance after rigorous training in banking, or started in accounting and grown into a broader role. Most importantly, you own outcomes. When something important falls between functions, your instinct is to understand it, fix it, and build a system so it stays fixed. All with a mindset of making complexity disappear and avoiding unnecessary process. We offer The opportunity to work at the vanguard of AI research and frontier biology, with world-class people, on a mission that matters. We protect & promote a culture of high velocity and ownership. We compensate our team accordingly.

title: CX Operations Enablement Specialist
description:
Who we are

The real world is the next frontier, and at Metropolis, we are creating the artificial intelligence to make it responsive. We are pioneering the Recognition Economy — a future where mundane repetition disappears and being known unlocks access, comfort, and belonging everywhere you go. From transforming parking into a seamless drive-in, drive-out experience for millions of Members to expanding our intelligence layer across retail and hospitality, we are building a world that feels instinctive and magical. The future isn’t coming; it’s here, and we need builders, innovators, and problem solvers to help us create it.

Who you are

Metropolis is seeking a CX Operations Enablement Specialist to serve as the operational translator and steward of our Customer Experience knowledge ecosystem. In this role, you will tear down process friction, embed our "Trust-First" support philosophy, and ensure our frontline human agents and AI support tools have access to highly accurate, empathetic, and actionable information. Partnering closely with Operations, Product, QA, Training, and AI Strategy teams, you will architect SOPs, manage our knowledge libraries, and empower support teams to drive First Contact Resolution (FCR) and deliver exceptional customer outcomes.

What you'll do

  • Serve as the operational owner of Customer Experience knowledge, managing the customer-facing Help Center and internal Knowledge Library
  • Lead the comprehensive teardown and rebuild of legacy SOPs, replacing rigid policies with workflows anchored in our core framework: Acknowledge, Empathize, Verify, Resolve
  • Build localized, compliant SOPs and decision trees for complex operational workflows, such as Dynamic Pricing disputes and 3rd-Party Reservation failures
  • Own, restructure, and maintain the Gladly CRM macro library (CX Answers) and FAQs to drive First Contact Resolution (FCR) while aligning with the Metropolis brand voice
  • Serve as the primary CX liaison to Operations Launch teams, ensuring localized knowledge assets and documentation are delivered prior to go-live for new locations
  • Act as the direct operational bridge to Experience Integrity and Government Relations to establish strictly compliant agent guardrails for regulatory-sensitive workflows
  • Structure organizational knowledge clearly so it can be effectively ingested and retrieved by our AI Agent (Parker) and internal LLMs
  • Partner with CX AI Content Analysts to close documentation gaps that cause AI hallucinations or routing failures
  • Conduct recurring knowledge audits to identify gaps, partnering with QA and Training to ensure operational alignment

What we're looking for

  • Experience managing or maintaining knowledge bases, help centers, or complex SOP documentation systems such as Gladly, Zendesk, Guru, or Confluence
  • Experience in Customer Support, Customer Experience, or a fast-paced operational environment
  • Strong technical writing, editing, and documentation skills with a hyper-focus on clarity, empathy, and usability
  • Ability to translate complex, localized operational and legal requirements into user-friendly documentation for frontline BPO agents
  • Strong project management skills, specifically in driving cross-functional alignment ahead of strict launch deadlines
  • Experience leveraging AI tools to transform static workflows into responsive, high-output processes

While not required, these are a plus:

  • Experience supporting AI-powered customer support solutions or familiarity with generative AI tools like Claude, Gemini, or ChatGPT
  • Experience with Gladly, Zendesk, Intercom, or similar CRM platforms
  • Experience creating customer support documentation at scale
  • Understanding of information architecture, content strategy, and knowledge management best practices

4 Days in Office: Metropolis values in-person collaboration to drive innovation, strengthen culture, and enhance the Member experience. Our corporate team members hold to our office-first model, which requires employees to be on-site at least four days a week, fostering organic interactions that spark creativity and connection

When you join Metropolis, you'll join a team of world-class product leaders and engineers, building an ecosystem of technologies at the intersection of parking, mobility, and real estate. Our goal is to build an inclusive culture where everyone has a voice and the best idea wins. You will play a key role in building and maintaining this culture as our organization grows. The anticipated base salary for this position is $63,000.00 USD to $75,000.00 USD annually. The actual base salary offered is determined by a number of variables, including, as appropriate, the applicant's qualifications for the position, years of relevant experience, distinctive skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location of residence and/or place of employment. Base salary is one component of Metropolis' total compensation package, which may also include access to or eligibility for healthcare benefits, a 401(k) plan, short-term and long-term disability coverage, basic life insurance, a lucrative stock option plan, bonus plans, and more. #LI-AW1 #LI-Onsite

Metropolis may utilize an automated employment decision tool (AEDT) to assess or evaluate your candidacy for employment or promotion. AEDTs are used to assist in assessing a candidate’s application relative to the required job qualifications and responsibilities listed in the job posting.

As part of this process, Metropolis retains data relevant to your candidacy, including personal information, for a period that is reasonably necessary for the use of the tool. If you are hired for the position, your data may become part of your employee records.

Metropolis Technologies is an equal opportunity employer. We make all hiring decisions based on merit, qualifications, and business needs — without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy), national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law.

We are committed to providing a welcoming, accessible hiring experience. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or interview process, please reach out to us at recruiting@metropolis.io.

title: Lead Front End Architect/Engineer
description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry Media is transforming how medical and healthcare marketers engage healthcare professionals (HCPs) and consumers through data, technology, and omnichannel innovation. Real Chemistry Media's product and technology teams sit at the heart of this meaningful work by building tools that increase impact. In support of our mission to help life-changing medicines and therapies reach their full market potential, we are building an enterprise platform for omnichannel orchestration in healthcare marketing.

Our technology enables healthcare organizations to design, deploy, and optimize HCP journeys through a scalable, self-service product that connects to their existing marketing and data systems. The platform is live with early users and on track with rapid growth milestones, so the decisions made over the next year will be influential in shaping the product's future.

We are hiring a Lead Engineer, Front End to lead the architecture and hands-on delivery of the interfaces our customers use to build and manage HCP journeys. You will lead front-end engineering, hire and grow the team behind it, and partner closely with the back end lead and product designer so the platform's interface, data model, and design system evolve together. The team is small and we're building a lot, so there are a lot of opportunities for ownership and influence.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead front-end architecture and hands-on delivery for the platform's user-facing product, from early prototypes through production.
  • Lead the journey-builder canvas — a direct-manipulation, graph-based interface — as it scales to more complex journeys and larger data volumes.
  • Define API contracts together with the back end lead, so the interface and the data model evolve as one system.
  • Drive the code side of the design system and the design-to-code workflow, in partnership with the product designer, who leads the design system itself.
  • Direct how AI-driven guardrails and model behavior are rendered and made trustworthy in the product.
  • Hire and lead a front-end engineering team as it grows, setting a high bar for code quality and CI-enforced testing.
  • Support and set standards for agentic coding on your team, backed by real company investment in the tools, not just tolerance for their use.
  • Partner with product and design on problem definition, scope, and sequencing from the start of each effort.

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.
  • You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines.

What You Should Have:

  • 8+ years in front-end or full-stack engineering, including 2+ years leading a team.
  • Experience leading front-end architecture for a B2B or enterprise product, ideally one with a complex, data-dense, or direct-manipulation UI (a canvas, graph editor, or similar).
  • Track record hiring and growing engineers, and running a technical interview loop from scratch.
  • Comfortable directing and reviewing agentic or AI-assisted coding, with the judgment to know what to hold to human review regardless of how the code was produced.
  • Fluency defining and maintaining API contracts across a team boundary.
  • Ability to turn ambiguous product problems into a sequenced, shippable technical plan.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and a fast-moving, still-small engineering org.
  • Bonus points for pharma or HCP marketing experience — or any complex, regulated marketing data environment (ad tech, financial services marketing, health systems).

 

Pay Range: $175,000-$200,000

This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time. 

Real Chemistry is proud to be Great Place to Work® certified; check out what our people shared about our culture and workplace on our Great Places to Work Profile here.

We believe we can do our best when feeling our best, which is why we’ve put together a benefits program designed to give you the support you and your family need at every stage of life. description: Risk and Controls Operations Associate Office Location: Temple, London - hybrid working environment (3 days in office per week) Reporting: Chief Operating Officer About Investa Investa is building the UK’s first zero-commission Options and Stocks trading platform. Legacy platforms typically feature high fees and complex interfaces that cut out the majority of retail investors. We are building a streamlined alternative to fix that. So far, we have raised £3.5 million in funding, secured direct regulatory approval from the FCA, and picked up two major awards in 2026: Best Options Trading App (Good Money Guide) and Best App for Options Trading (ADVFN). Having launched on iOS - reaching 4,000+ total sign-ups - we have now just launched on Android, doubling our addressable market as we scale toward targets of 10,000 users, 100,000, and beyond. Key Platform Traction: 8,000+ trades processed 2,500+ early supporters rewarded for their loyalty 1,000+ shareholders backing our vision 150+ 5-star reviews Our goal is straightforward: Think Options, Think Investa. We are a lean, agile team where every employee directly shapes the business. We don't have a corporate way of working. Instead, we look for people who want high autonomy, care about making a visible impact, and align with our core values of being Collaborative, Curious, and Creative. The Role As our Risk & Controls Operations Associate, you will serve as the first line of regulatory and operational control for Investa’s platform. Working together with our Head of Risk & Compliance and Co-Founders, you will help own the day-to-day execution of our key operational controls spanning CASS oversight, onboarding operations, financial crime monitoring, and execution control. This is a critical, high-visibility role within a fast-scaling financial trading environment. You will bridge regulatory oversight with practical execution: verifying client money flows, resolving dealing and onboarding exceptions, and ensuring our operations adhere strictly to FCA standards as our operating model expands from sub-account clearing into in-house custody. What the role involves 1. Risk & Control Operations CASS Reconciliations: Perform daily internal & external CASS reconciliations across Investa’s client base to prevent breaches and ensure compliance with day-to-day CASS obligations. CASS Reporting & Audits: Maintain audit-ready compliance records, log breaks and CASS breaches, and assist in preparing regulatory returns and notifications when needed. KYC & Onboarding Operations: Own the day-to-day onboarding queue, performing KYC/AML document reviews, appropriateness assessments, and managing PEPs, sanctions, and high-risk escalations. Financial Crime Monitoring: Organise high-risk client reviews assisting with enhanced due diligence, source of funds/wealth checks, and periodic and event driven reviews. Vulnerable Customer Framework: Manage sensitive customer cases as identified in the vulnerable clients policy, ensure good outcomes for clients with support needs, manage key performance indicators for clients in this segment in strict compliance with Consumer Duty standards and internal policies. 2. Business Oversight & Governance Support Management Information: Own and gather key performance indicators covering all aspects of the business for committee reporting and oversight. Financial Promotions: Review and approve marketing campaigns, product copy, and social media promotions to ensure strict alignment with FCA Financial Promotion and Consumer Duty rules. Regulatory Change: Assist in implementation of regulatory change in the UK or elsewhere to ensure compliance with new rules that apply to the Firm. Third Party Risk Management: Point of contact for vendors and outsourcing partners to oversee and coordinate information sharing for incident closure & customer support. Trade surveillance: Provide first line review of alerts generated through trade surveillance for signs of market abuse. Oversee the closure of alerts and applicable audit trail. Your Background 2+ years of hands-on experience covering trade operations or controls support at a regulated firm, FinTech, investment platform, or broker. Understanding of the regulatory framework surrounding CASS, Consumer Duty, Systems & Controls, and Anti-Money Laundering. Direct experience executing CASS reconciliation workflows, client adoption, and trade surveillance. Strong analytical mindset with high attention to detail and sound, practical judgement. Technical proficiency in Office and Google-based software including excel, Google Sheets, Google Docs. Desirable Prior exposure to retail investment platforms, derivatives markets. Experience using workflow tools like Jira or case management software. Familiarity with third-party clearing integrations (e.g., Interactive Brokers) or regulatory reporting tools. CISI or equivalent qualification regarding financial services, client assets, or regulatory modules. Understanding of EU regulation. What we offer Career Ownership & Impact: You have autonomy over your execution and your career trajectory. Your work impacts the business immediately without corporate red tape. You can choose whether you want to pave a path as a high-level individual contributor or step into management as we scale - you shape your career. Collaboration & Proximity: You work alongside our co-founders. Because of our size, our culture is extremely personal. title: Manager, Human Resources Operations, Japan
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Revolution Medicines is seeking a Manager, Human Resources (HR) Operations, Japan to lead the delivery of reliable, consistent, and efficient employee services and HR processes. This people-manager role oversees the day-to-day work of the HR Operations team, translates functional plans into scalable workflows, and resolves operational issues across the employee lifecycle. Reporting to the Director, Human Rescources, Japan, the manager partners closely with HR, Payroll, Finance, Legal, Compliance, IT and other key stakeholders to deliver timely, accurate, and compliant HR services (dotted line reporting to the Senior Director, People Operations and Technology in the US).

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead employee lifecycle operations, including onboarding, employee changes, leave coordination, and offboarding, and ensure accurate and timely service.

  • Translate HR policies and functional priorities into documented procedures, controls, service standards, and teamwork plans.

  • Manage HR information system workflows, data quality, reporting, and issue resolution in partnership with HR, Payroll, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications and IT.

  • Coordinate HR operations vendors, monitor service performance and operating expenses, and address service risks and escalations.

  • Track service metrics and employee feedback, identify recurring issues, and lead continuous improvement of HR operations processes to increase quality, compliance, efficiency, and scalability.

  • Lead the responsible use of technology, including AI and automation, to simplify workflows, reduce manual effort, and improve data quality and employee service in partnership with HR, IT, Legal, and data privacy stakeholders.

  • Represent HR Operations in cross-functional and regional or global projects by defining requirements, coordinating dependencies, managing implementation activities, and supporting adoption.

  • Set team goals, assign work, coach team members, support professional development, and reinforce accountability for service delivery.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.

  • A minimum of six years of progressive HR operations experience, including at least two years leading employees or significant operational workstreams.

  • Strong knowledge of employee lifecycle processes, HR systems, data controls, and service delivery.

  • Working knowledge of applicable Japanese employment requirements and employee data privacy practices.

  • Experience managing operational projects, vendors, expenses, and cross-functional dependencies.

  • Strong analytical judgment, problem-solving skills, and clear written and verbal communication.

  • Native-level Japanese and business-level English proficiency, with the ability to communicate clearly with employees, leaders, vendors, and global partners.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience in biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, or another regulated, high-growth environment.

  • Experience with Workday or a comparable enterprise HR platform.

  • Experience supporting multi-state or global employee populations.

title: Peer Review Operations Specialist - 2 Year FTC
description:
This position is fully remote/home based. Applications will be accepted from candidates based in the UK. This is a 2 Year FTC.

Role Summary

As a Peer Review Operations Specialist, you are a confident and highly organized self-starter, motivated by a culture of continuous improvement. You’re an excellent communicator and a natural team player, with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams and hold yourself accountable for meeting competing deadlines in a fast-paced environment. 

Reporting to the Peer Review Operations Manager, you work as a member of the Peer Review Operations team to maintain efficient peer review workflows, ensure high vendor performance standards, and uphold excellent contributor experience for authors, editors, and reviewers. You will enforce turnaround time benchmarks for all peer review milestones to protect process integrity and ensure timeliness and quality of publication. You will have high standards of professional conduct in the workplace, and enjoy working with international colleagues from a range of cultures and settings. You will seek out opportunities for continuous quality improvement in department activities and be an effective champion of the PLOS vision, mission, and brand.

Responsibilities

Submission Management 

  • Ensure the timely, efficient peer review of all submissions
  • Ensure that queries or concerns escalated by vendors, Customer Care or other PLOS colleagues are addressed and resolved professionally and within required timelines, or escalated appropriately
  • Identify and remove barriers to submission, working collaboratively with colleagues across PLOS as required
  • Proactively identify workflow inefficiencies, variations or backlogs to diagnose persistent issues 
  • Ensure that manuscripts meet requirements and follow current policies and procedures

Workflows 

  • Troubleshoot persistent manuscript, workflow or system issues, providing expertise and advice, and exercising judgement to resolve the issue or escalate to the Peer Review Operations Manager or other colleagues as appropriate
  • Proactively raise data-driven recommendations for continuous journal operations and workflow improvements to the Peer Review Operations Manager
  • Ensure standard journal workflows are maintained as established, implementing and adopting process updates when approved by the Peer Review Operations Manager

Projects 

  • Contribute to workflow project and initiate proposals as requested, and undertake operations projects and initiatives as directed by the Peer Review Operations Manager
  • Serve as daily liaison with vendor representatives, monitoring quality and timeliness performance against target thresholds and KPIs

Other 

  • Contribute to other operational research outputs related to PLOS’s mission where required, so that our journal workflows are optimised to encourage scientific openness and transparency

Knowledge and Skills

Essential

  • Prior experience in peer-reviewed schololarly publishing
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, both written and oral
  • Growth mindset with a collaborative, team player mentality
  • An ability to maintain a positive and professional customer service attitude
  • Able to work constructively with vendors, authors, editors, customers, and colleagues from a range of international settings
  • Knowledge of Excel, Word, file types and file conversions
  • Able to work under tight deadlines whilst achieving a high standard of quality and accuracy
  • Able to set priorities and work independently
  • Upholds high standards of professionalism in the workplace
  • Embraces change with a positive attitude
  • An interest in science and in advancing scientific knowledge

Desirable

  • Knowledge of and expertise with peer review and manuscript management database systems; proficiency with Editorial Manager a plus
  • Knowledge of customer relationship management (CRM) software such as Salesforce
  • Awareness of and commitment to open science

Physical Requirements and Work Environment

  • Prolonged periods stationary at a desk and working on a computer.
  • Some domestic and international travel required.

Qualifications

  • A university degree or equivalent experience 

 

The base salary range we've established for these positions is £27,000- £30,000. PLOS also offers a comprehenseive benefits package sumarized below.

BENEFITS: 

US:

  • 401k with employer match
  • Employee sponsored health, dental and vision insurance (Dental and Vision 100% employer paid)
  • Paid Vacation, 11 public holidays and sick leave
  • Parental leave
  • Birthday and three winter holidays days off
  • Short term and long term disability insurance
  • 2 days paid time off for volunteering per year
  • Fully remote work environment with stipend on joining for home office 

 

About PLOS 

Building on a strong legacy of pioneering innovation, PLOS continues to be a catalyst in open science, reimagining models to meet open science principles, removing barriers and promoting inclusion in knowledge creation and sharing, and publishing research outputs that enable everyone to learn from, reuse and build upon scientific knowledge.

Our work is supported by a highly skilled global in-house team, partnerships with local scholarly organizations, and the valued contributions of a diverse, international community of scientific researchers.

We’re committed to equal opportunity

We’re working to create a more equitable system of scientific knowledge and understanding. Removing barriers to inclusion and facilitating broad participation of voices is core to our success, inside and out. 

Beyond accepting distinct perspectives, we seek and support divergent backgrounds among our staff because we know differences strengthen our teams, our work, and our communities. We strongly encourage applicants of all identities to join us as we work towards a future where science is open to all, for all. 

Visit plos.org/careers to learn more.

title: Business Analyst
description:
About Avalere Health

United by one profound purpose: to reach EVERY PATIENT POSSIBLE. At Avalere Health, we ensure every patient is identified, treated, supported, and cared for. Equally. Our Advisory, Medical, and Marketing teams come together – powerfully and intentionally – to forge unconventional connections, building a future where healthcare is not a barrier and no patient is left behind. 

Achieving our mission starts with providing enriching, purpose-driven careers for our team that empower them to make a tangible impact on patient lives. We are committed to creating a culture where our employees are empowered to bring their whole selves to work and tap into the power of diverse backgrounds and skillsets to play a part in making a difference for every patient, everywhere. 

Our flexible approach to working allows our global teams to decide where they want to work, whether in-office or at home based on team and client need. Major city hubs in London, Manchester, Washington, D.C., and New York, and smaller offices globally, serve as collaboration hubs allowing our teams to come together when it matters. Homeworkers are equally supported, with dedicated social opportunities and resources.  

Our inclusive culture is at the heart of everything we do. We proudly support our employees in bringing their whole selves to work with our six Employee Network Groups – Diverse Ability, Family, Gender, LGBTQ+, Mental Health, and Race/Ethnicity. These groups provide opportunities to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion and to connect, learn, and socialise through regular meetings and programs of activity. We are an accredited Fertility Friendly employer with our Fertility Policy, enhanced parental leave, and culture of flexibility ensuring every employee feels supported across their family planning journey and can work in a way that suits their family’s needs. 

We are deeply invested in supporting professional growth for our employees through day-to-day career experiences, access to thousands of on-demand training sessions, regular career conversations, and the opportunity for global, cross-capability career moves.  

We take pride in being part of the Disability Confident Scheme. This helps make sure you can be interviewed fairly if you have a disability, long term health condition, or are neurodiverse. If you'd like to apply and need adjustments made, you can let us know in your application.
 What we can offer You will receive a 401K plan with an employer match contribution up to 4% (immediately vested), as well as life insurance, disability coverage, and medical, dental, and vision plans for peace of mind. Enjoy flexible working arrangements, including hybrid and remote work, along with the option to work from anywhere across the globe two weeks each year. We provide 20 vacation days plus one personal well-being day, recognise 9 public holidays, along with gifted end-of-year holidays and an early Summer Friday finish in June, July, and August. Access free counselling through our employee assistance program and personalized health support. Our enhanced maternity, paternity, family leave, and fertility policies provide support across every stage of your family-planning journey. You can also benefit from continuous opportunities to professionally develop with on-demand training, support, and global mobility opportunities across the business. We encourage all applicants to read our candidate privacy notice before applying to Avalere Health.

title: Small to Midsize Strategy Leader - Clinical Data
description:
Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
 
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
 
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
 
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.


The Role
Veeva Systems is seeking a Strategy Leader responsible for growing the Clinical Data business with the world’s leading pharmaceutical companies.
 
The small and medium-sized business (SMB) Strategy Leader of Clinical Data requires a familiarity with clinical research and/or healthcare data flow. The SMB Clinical Data Strategy Leader must demonstrate the ability to drive adoption discussions based on credibility and knowledge across multiple domains, including pharma/biotech, CRO, and technology partnership. The SMB Clinical Data Strategy Leader must demonstrate the ability to challenge customers to adopt new operating models and change their traditional way of thinking.
 
Vault Clinical Data comprises Electronic Data Capture (EDC) and Data Quality System (DQS). This role will be responsible for driving Clinical Data market strategy and growth across our emerging and mid-size  customers, working with the sales team, ensuring customer success, and developing a tailored market approach for customers with small internal teams. To achieve these goals the Strategy Leader of Clinical Data will need to connect with clinical and data management leaders, clinical operations leaders and IT leadership to create strategic plans that deliver and demonstrate customer success, and work directly with sales to identify and win opportunities to grow the business.
 
In this role, you will have the opportunity to work with a team of industry and technology leaders, who, together, are bringing the next generation of clinical development and R&D applications to Life Sciences.
 
This position can be based anywhere in North America.
 #LI-Remote #LI-Director Veeva’s headquarters is located in the San Francisco Bay Area with offices in more than 15 countries around the world. Veeva is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, national origin or ancestry, age, disability, marital status, pregnancy, protected veteran status, protected genetic information, political affiliation, or any other characteristics protected by local laws, regulations, or ordinances. If you need assistance or accommodation due to a disability or special need when applying for a role or in our recruitment process, please contact us at talent_accommodations@veeva.com.

title: Solutions Delivery Manager
description: We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era. When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. title: Lead Back End Architect/Engineer
description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry Media is transforming how medical and healthcare marketers engage healthcare professionals (HCPs) and consumers through data, technology, and omnichannel innovation. Real Chemistry Media's product and technology teams sit at the heart of this meaningful work by building tools that increase impact. In support of our mission to help life-changing medicines and therapies reach their full market potential, we are building an enterprise platform for omnichannel orchestration in healthcare marketing.

Our technology enables healthcare organizations to design, deploy, and optimize HCP journeys through a scalable, self-service product that connects to their existing marketing and data systems. The platform is live with early users and on track with rapid growth milestones, so the decisions made over the next year will be influential in shaping the product's future.

We are hiring a Lead Engineer, Back End to drive the services and data model that power the platform. You will lead back-end architecture and hands-on delivery, hire and grow a team of back-end and data engineers, and direct how the platform's data scales, stays reliable, and connects to the systems around it. The team is small and we're building a lot, so there are a lot of opportunities for ownership and influence.

What You'll Do:

  • Lead the platform's application data model in Aurora and DynamoDB, and the access-pattern decisions behind it, as the product scales.
  • Drive the integration contract with our data warehouse — what flows each way, on what cadence — and keep the warehouse out of the platform's request path.
  • Define API contracts together with the front end lead, so the interface and the data model evolve as one system.
  • Direct the reliability, performance, and cost of back-end services, partnering with DevOps on the platform-level non-functional requirements that take both teams' input.
  • Partner with data science to productionize the models and recommendation features built on top of the platform's data.
  • Hire and lead a team of back-end and data engineers, setting a high bar for code quality and CI-enforced testing.
  • Support and set standards for agentic coding on your team, backed by real company investment in the tools, not just tolerance for their use.
  • Partner with product and design on problem definition, scope, and sequencing from the start of each effort.

 

This position is a perfect fit for you if:

  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.
  • You are highly organized self-starter, able to work independently and under tight deadlines.

 

What You Should Have:

  • 8+ years in back-end or full-stack engineering, including 2+ years leading a team.
  • Experience leading a data model and access patterns for a B2B or enterprise product at meaningful scale, ideally across both a relational and a NoSQL store.
  • Track record hiring and growing engineers, and running a technical interview loop from scratch.
  • Comfortable directing and reviewing agentic or AI-assisted coding, with the judgment to know what to hold to human review regardless of how the code was produced.
  • Experience partnering with data science or ML teams to get models into production.
  • Fluency defining and maintaining API contracts across a team boundary.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and a fast-moving, still-small engineering org.
  • Bonus points for pharma or HCP marketing experience — or any complex, regulated marketing data environment (ad tech, financial services marketing, health systems).

 

Pay Range: $175,000-$200,000

This is the pay range the Company believes it will pay for this position at the time of this posting.  Consistent with applicable law, compensation will be determined based on job-related, non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, skills, certifications, and geographical location. The Company reserves the right to modify this pay range at any time.

Other perks include mental wellness coaching and support and access to more than 13,000 online classes with LinkedIn Learning.  Learn more about our great benefits and perks and search specific offerings in your region at: www.realchemistrybenefits.com.

title: In Vivo Research Associate II, Konermann Lab
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

We are seeking an In Vivo Research Associate II to join the Konermann Laboratory at the Arc Institute.You will collaborate closely with experienced scientists to advance in vivo projects focused on understanding brain development.

This project builds on previous work in genome-scale CRISPR screening (Konermann et al., 2015; Biering et al., 2021; Wei et al., 2023; Roohani et al., 2025) and aims to combine modern functional genomics and neuroscience tools to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying brain development and function. The ideal candidate will have experience in animal handling and colony management, intracerebral injections, sample processing for single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial pipelines, and imaging. This position offers an excellent opportunity for candidates considering PhD programs, as it involves participation in all stages of a research project under the guidance of an experienced scientist.

About You

  • You love science and learning. Whether it's a new field or a new bench technique, you stay curious and enjoy stepping outside your comfort zone.
  • You are detail-oriented. You're careful and diligent about documentation and good lab practice, and you like keeping things organized.
  • You collaborate and help others. Science is a team effort, and you take the initiative to pitch in.
  • You are a problem solver. Experiments rarely work the first time. You bring patience and confidence to complex technical troubleshooting.

 In this position, you will

  • Plan, execute, analyze, and troubleshoot experiments with a high degree of independence, with continued support from the rest of the team
  • Perform in vivo mouse experiments, including stereotaxic surgeries, as well as IV and IP injections
  • Collect and process tissue, including vibratome and/or cryostat sectioning, immunostaining, and imaging
  • Comply with federal, Arc, and local IACUC/AAALAC regulations governing animal research
  • Follow Arc's standards for code of conduct, safety, and the handling of hazardous materials, biological materials, and controlled substances
  • Analyze and present data at subgroup meetings and seminars
  • Maintain an organized, detailed lab notebook

Job Requirements

  • BS with 2+ years of relevant experience, or MS, in molecular biology, neuroscience, or another relevant field. Relevant experience includes independent lab work during undergraduate studies
  • Strong experience working with laboratory animals, including handling, restraint, and procedures under an approved protocol (intracranial, IV, and IP injections, as well as perfusions)
  • Detail-oriented, with excellent organizational and time-management skills
  • Outstanding critical thinking and problem-solving skills
  • Strong oral and written communication skills
  • Highly motivated and curious, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a collaborative team
  • Ability to work some weekends as needed (days off can be swapped for weekdays

Preferred Skills

  • Prior experience with cloning via Gibson assembly or Golden Gate protocols (library cloning experience is a plus)
  • Knowledge of and experience with NGS library preparation, particularly single-cell and spatial workflows
  • Computational skills (Python or R)

The base salary for this position is $75,900. This amount does not include benefits or other forms of compensation.

title: Technical Advisor, Surveillance, Data Use and Decision Science (Remote - Kinshasa, DRC)
description:
Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL) is a global health organization that partners locally and globally to create and scale solutions to the world’s deadliest health threats. Millions of people die from preventable health threats. We collaborate to close the gap between proven, life-saving solutions and the people who need them. Since 2017, we’ve worked with governments and other partners in more than 60 countries to save millions of lives. We work toward a future where people live longer, healthier lives, communities flourish, and economies thrive. This is an ambitious vision, and it inspires us and our partners to make progress every day. 

Resolve to Save Lives' Prevent Epidemics program works closely with Ministries of Health and national public health institutes in Africa to strengthen epidemic preparedness capacity, accelerate disease detection and response, and effectively use data to inform action. In addition to direct partnerships with governments, we also work with implementing partners, including the US CDC, the World Health Organization, the World Bank, and the Global Health Advocacy Incubator, to implement programs, prototype innovations, and ensure sustainability through increased national ownership, including domestic budget allocations.

Position Purpose:  

RTSL is seeking a Technical Advisor for Surveillance, Data Use and Decision Science. This position aims to strengthen collaboration, governance, and the use of public health data to improve disease surveillance at the national and subnational levels. The advisor will provide technical support to the structures responsible for surveillance in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), including the National Public Health Institute (INSP), its Public Health Emergency Operations Center (COUSP), the Directorate of Epidemiological Surveillance (DSE), disease control programs, and the National Institute of Biomedical Research (INRB), in order to use data to detect threats, track alerts, analyze 7-1-7 timelines, and guide public health decisions. They will develop simple, useful information products, train teams, and help identify delays in detection, notification, investigation, confirmation, and early response. 

The position will be a part of the RTSL DRC team and will support national institutions, without substituting for their mandates. The Technical Advisor will work with national technical teams and contribute to the development of simple, useful, and prioritized information products. They will train teams and help identify delays in detection, notification, investigation, confirmation, and early response — particularly weekly epidemiological reports, situation reports or investigated events, as well as 7-1-7 analyses, epidemiological bulletins, and risk information products — in order to support decision-making that strengthens preparedness, response, and health security in the DRC. They will benefit from RTSL's technical support. 

This is a one-year, renewable fixed-term contract with a 3-month probationary period. 

Core Duties and Responsibilities: 

Responsibilities will cover the full data lifecycle, including but not limited to: 

Technical Support & Mentorship: 

  • Collaborate with directors and decision-makers responsible for public health emergency management to identify data needs for decision-making 
  • Provide direct coaching and technical assistance to relevant INSP staff responsible for developing priority information products, including 7-1-7 dashboards, based on consensus and approval from relevant managers 
  • Identify bottlenecks related to the sharing, governance, and use of data relevant to public health emergency preparedness and response, and collaborate with relevant departments to address and resolve these challenges 
  • Provide guidance, technical mentoring, and capacity-building support to INSP staff and other stakeholders in data management, analysis, visualization, and interpretation, particularly the 7-1-7 detection, notification, investigation, confirmation, and early response timelines 
  • Strengthen capacities in data analysis and visualization, including statistical modeling and real-time dashboards, aiming to improve surveillance reporting and outbreak response through mentoring and structured training 
  • Support the prioritization and design of information products among various stakeholders, both within INSP and with other national surveillance structures 
  • Collaborate with INSP teams, surveillance structures, and RTSL teams working on data architecture to support initiatives aimed at improving data governance and coordination of public health emergency management 
  • Support the translation and implementation of data structures to promote data use and automation of data processing pipelines 
  • Provide technical support for the development of strategic documents and guidelines aimed at improving the national surveillance architecture and data governance  

Development of Information Products: 

  • Support staff at surveillance structures, including INSP, and relevant stakeholders in developing or improving key data products, particularly weekly epidemiological reports, epidemiological bulletins, situation reports, and risk information products  
  • Contribute to improving data visualization dashboards, predictive analysis models, and automated reporting systems to strengthen disease surveillance and risk assessment  
  • Ensure alignment of data products with the One Health approach 

Data-Driven Decision-Making & Capacity Building: 

  • Analyze 7-1-7 data related to detection, notification, investigation, confirmation, and early response initiation. Produce useful insights to guide decisions, identify bottlenecks, and prioritize activation of the rapid response fund  
  • Support INSP in transforming surveillance data, epidemiological data, and 7-1-7 data into actionable insights for public health decision-making  
  • Identify capacity-building needs for data use, including staff training in basic epidemiology, R, data science, and data analysis  
  • Organize training workshops, seminars, and hands-on sessions for staff at surveillance structures including INSP, DSE, INRB, disease control programs, provincial teams, and health zone epidemiologists to strengthen their analytical skills  
  • Facilitate the development and implementation of a data use strategy to improve the quality, accessibility, and usefulness of health data for better decision-making 

 Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration: 

  • Support activities to strengthen regular sharing of data useful for epidemic and pandemic preparedness and response, among surveillance structures including INSP, DSE, INRB, disease control programs, provincial teams, other sectors, ministries, departments, and agencies  
  • Identify opportunities for collaboration and support among surveillance structures including INSP, DSE, INRB, disease control programs, provincial teams, and other ministries, departments, and agencies to improve data sharing and use, as well as synergies in preparedness, epidemic response, and implementation of the 7-1-7 approach  
  • Provide technical support and facilitate stakeholder engagement for new or existing initiatives aimed at improving data governance and coordination  
  • Facilitate support for processes and workflows, including support for regular meetings of routine surveillance and emergency preparedness teams, such as EIR, EMU, and technical working groups  
  • Support meetings focused on data sharing and data product innovations, as well as multisectoral workshops focused on joint data projects and data-sharing agreements  
  • Carry out any other related tasks assigned by RTSL 

Required Qualifications:  

Education:  

  • Master’s or PhD in Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Data Science, Public Health, Health Informatics, or a related field 
  • Proficiency in English is a strong asset 

Experience: 

  • Minimum of 8 years of experience in public health or related discipline in health data analytics, disease surveillance, or decision science, preferably within a public health or government agency 
  • Demonstrated experience in capacity-building, training, and mentorship of public health professionals 

Skills & competencies: 

  • Strong understanding of public health, data compilation, management, and analysis, including understanding of public health informatics and the importance of data in supporting health surveillance and emergency management 
  • Advanced R skills, including data preparation, descriptive statistics, data visualization, geospatial mapping 
  • Intermediate proficiency in R Shiny and Quarto or Markdown for creating interactive applications and automated reports

title: Product Manager, Platform
description: We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era. When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done. Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma. We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today. ROLE OVERVIEW AI is only as good as the data underneath it. Schemas is the configuration layer where customers model their scientific data and processes. It's the customer-defined data model that makes Benchling different from a point solution, and the contract every other system (internal apps, integrations, AI agents) relies on when reading or writing to Benchling. Get it right, and AI inherits a solid foundation; get it wrong, every layer above inherits the problem. As Schemas PM, you own the primitives (schema types, computed fields, fieldsets, constraints, static properties, data versioning) that every other team at Benchling builds on top of. This is one of the highest-leverage, most technically interesting roles on the platform team, and one we're investing in now as AI features across Benchling increasingly depend on the quality of the underlying data model. RESPONSIBILITIES Set product direction for Schemas and ship toward it incrementally, balancing fast prototyping with the platform stability admins and developers depend on. Relentlessly track how customers use Schemas — where it delights, where it fails — and build sharp personas and job-to-be-done context for each user type (admins, scientists, computational teams, internal and external developers). Bring customer "why," not just feature requests, back to Engineering and Design; partner with them closely to ship new capabilities. Champion structured, well-modeled data as the foundation for AI value across Benchling, anticipating what schema consumers will need next. Partner with Customer Experience, Field, Sales, and Marketing to get customer signal into the roadmap early. Partner closely with other Platform and Apps PMs — schemas underpin nearly every other platform surface, so alignment on sequencing and shared abstractions matters as much as your own roadmap. QUALIFICATIONS Energized by platform work and systems thinking; comfortable building the right abstraction ahead of need. Has designed, owned, or significantly evolved a data-modeling, schema, or configuration system used by external developers or technical admins — not just consumed one as a feature. Becomes the go-to person for customers, field, and engineers — not a router to engineering. Deep, demonstrated discovery practice: has built personas and JTBD frameworks from scratch, not just used ones handed to them. Track record balancing long-term vision with incremental shipping. Strong communicator across technical and executive audiences; B2B SaaS or developer-platform background preferred. Genuine curiosity about the science behind the data. You don't need a science background, but you should want one by the end of your first quarter here. HOW WE WORK Flexible Hybrid Work: We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. #LI-EK1 Benchling welcomes everyone. We believe diversity enriches our team so we hire people with a wide range of identities, backgrounds, and experiences. We are an equal opportunity employer. That means we don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We also consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including but not limited to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

title: Candidate Experience Coordinator, Cambridge, MA
description:
Isomorphic Labs is applying frontier AI to help unlock deeper scientific insights, faster breakthroughs, and life-changing medicines with an ambition to solve all disease.

The future is coming. A future enabled and enriched by the incredible power of machine learning. A future in which diseases are curtailed or cured starting with better and faster drug discovery. 

Come and be part of an interdisciplinary team driving groundbreaking innovation and play a meaningful role in contributing towards us achieving our ambitious goals, while being a part of an inspiring and collaborative culture.

The world we want tomorrow is the one we’re building today. It starts with the culture at this company. It starts with you. 

 

About Iso

Isomorphic Labs (IsoLabs) was launched in 2021 to advance human health by building on and beyond the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system. Since then, our interdisciplinary team of drug discovery experts and machine learning specialists has built powerful new predictive and generative AI models that accelerate scientific discovery at digital speed.

Our name comes from the belief that there is an underlying symmetry between biology and information science. By harnessing AI’s powerful capabilities, we can use it to model complex biological phenomena to help design novel molecules, anticipate how drugs will perform and develop innovative medicines to treat and cure some of the world’s most devastating diseases.

We have built a world-leading drug design engine comprising AI models that are capable of working across multiple therapeutic areas and drug modalities. We are continually innovating on model architecture and developing cutting-edge capabilities to advance rational drug design.

Every day, and with each new breakthrough, we’re getting closer to the promise of digital biology, and achieving our ambitious mission to one day solve all disease with the help of AI.

 

Your impact 

As a Candidate Experience Coordinator, you are the engine of our Talent Acquisition (TA) function. You won’t just support recruitment; you will architect, own, and lead the candidate journey through interdisciplinary collaboration.

Overseeing complex global scheduling, you will own the holistic end-to-end candidate experience— running an efficient and exceptional interview process from the first touchpoint to the final stages. You will drive data integrity to influence hiring decisions, whilst also serving as a process engineer who identifies bottlenecks and implements smoother workflows. This position is designed as a launchpad for your career, giving you interdisciplinary visibility and significant project ownership across the talent acquisition lifecycle.

What you will do 

1. Own the Candidate Experience Architecture

  • Curate the Journey: Act as a primary, consistent point of contact for candidates, ensuring every interaction is timely, seamless, and supportive. You will seamlessly balance high volume scheduling with candidate care.
  • Host the Onsite Experience: Act as the host and central lead for our onsite (or virtual) interview days, ensuring candidates feel welcomed, prepared, and impressed.
  • Humanise Communication: Partner across the team to design candidate communications. You will ensure our templates are authentic and aligned with our values, including managing early-stage rejections with empathy and professionalism.
  • Scheduling Excellence: Orchestrate complex, interdisciplinary interview loops across multiple time zones with speed and efficiency, proactively managing any last-minute changes with candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers.

2. Drive Operational Excellence & Data Integrity

  • Be a "Data Guardian”: Champion the quality and consistency of our data within our ATS (Greenhouse). You will manage job set up, build interview processes and ensure  candidate statuses are meticulously maintained to enable accurate reporting.

Onboarding Operations: Oversee critical onboarding and compliance operations, such as right-to-work checks, pobu (integrating people data with relevant google systems), and background checks. Upskill and educate the talent team on criticality of accurate data and Greenhouse (ATS) best practices in both hiring and onboarding processes.

  • Feedback Loops: Partner with the Principal Talent Lead to analyse candidate survey data. You will turn these insights into meaningful actions, blending data-driven and experiential perspectives to continuously elevate our standards.
  • Identify & Eradicate Bottlenecks: Proactively flag recurring scheduling challenges or process delays. You won’t just follow the process; you will help evolve it by suggesting improvements and piloting new workflows.

3. Enablement & Strategic Partnership

  • Scaling processes: Utilising AI, you will assist in documenting core processes for TA, creating clear and consistent guides for everything from complex scheduling to offer approval workflows. Additionally, you will ensure effective training for any new coordinators and wider TA members.
  • Champion Interdisciplinary Partnership: You will have opportunities for domain alignment with specific verticals, allowing you to build deeper context on the roles you support and partner closely with Hiring Managers, thereby leveraging diverse skills and perspectives across the business.

Skills and qualifications 

Essential:

  • Exceptional Organisation: Ability to prioritise multiple functions and tasks while maintaining the highest attention to detail in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience Centric: A strong focus on providing the best possible candidate experience, with the empathy to manage relationships through the entire recruitment lifecycle.
  • Tech & Data Savvy: Experience using online calendar/meeting applications (G-Suite preferred) and a data-driven approach with a strong desire to advocate for clean data.
  • Communication: Excellent communication skills, capable of keeping stakeholders updated and writing "human-first" correspondence.
  • Global Mindset: Experience scheduling and complex coordination across multiple time zones.
  • Process Mindset: The ability to learn complex systems quickly and a willingness to question "how things are done" to find better solutions.

Nice to have:

  • ATS Expertise: Deep experience with Applicant Tracking Systems, specifically Greenhouse
  • Project Management: Experience leading or contributing to operational projects (e.g., event logistics, data cleanup, survey rollouts).
  • Agency or Search Firm Experience: Experience acting as the main point of contact for external partners.


Culture and values

We are guided by our shared values. It's not about finding people who think and act in the same way. These values help to guide our work and will continue to strengthen it. 

Thoughtful
Thoughtful at Iso is about curiosity, creativity and care. It is about good people doing good, rigorous and future-making science every single day.

Brave
Brave at Iso is about fearlessness, but it’s also about initiative and integrity. The scale of the challenge demands nothing less.

Determined
Determined at Iso is the way we pursue our goal. It’s a confidence in our hypothesis, as well as the urgency and agility needed to deliver on it. Because disease won’t wait, so neither should we.

Together
Together at Iso is about connection, collaboration across fields and catalytic relationships. It’s knowing that transformation is a group project, and remembering that what we’re doing will have a real impact on real people everywhere.


Creating an extraordinary company

We believe that to be successful we need a team with a range of skills and talents. We're building an environment where collaboration is fundamental, learning is shared and every employee feels supported and able to thrive. We value unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, and perspectives, and harness these qualities to create extraordinary impact.

Hybrid working

It’s hugely important for us to share knowledge and build strong relationships with each other, and we find it easier to do this if we spend time together in person. The Accessioning Team Runner collects, sorts, and transports packages to Accessioning laboratory.   This position is located on site in our Austin, TX location.  Schedules listed below and pay starts at $17.    
 
Schedule:  Tuesday - Saturday, 10am-630pm 
  

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Sort and transport packages from the Shipping dock to the Accessioning laboratory.

  • Pick up packages from the receptionist’s desk.

  • Scan all tracking numbers into a Google spreadsheet and ensure that tracking numbers are scanned in correctly and spreadsheet is filled out completely.

  • Distribute packages to the Clinical Data Operators (CDO) in a timely and efficient manner following distribution guidelines.

  • Rack samples that arrive in bulk (without individual kit boxes) ensuring that the paperwork matches up with the samples.

  • Escalate any issues or discrepancies to the Leads or Supervisor.

  • Empty bins filled with kit boxes at the CDO workstations into carts placed at designated locations in the lab.

  • Perform a visual check of the kit boxes to make sure that there is no PHI on the kit boxes or samples remaining in the discarded kit boxes.

  • Empty biohazard cans in the lab.

  • Scan bench worksheets.

  • Scan documents into cases.

  • Maintain tidiness of Runner workstations.

  • Store requisition forms by date into the filing cabinets.

  • Dispose of requisition forms into the shred bins that have exceeded the retention period.

  • Performs other duties as assigned.

  • Notify Supervisor and Leads of any packaging issues or discrepancies

  • This role works with PHI on a regular basis both in paper and electronic form and has access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job

  • Employee must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire.

  • Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements.

 

QUALIFICATIONS

  • High School Diploma (or equivalent) required.

  • Previous computer experience.

  •  

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES

  • Familiar with Google documents.

  • Ability to perform basic calculations.

  • Organized and self- motivated.

  • Ability to work quickly and efficiently.
